Seattle by the numbers

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey counts about 741,440 people in Seattle, which makes it the 1st largest of the 51 Washington places we cover. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $912,100, 83% above the median of those 51 places. 44% of occupied homes are owner-occupied and 56% are rented, against a median of 59% owner-occupancy across the Washington places. The median home was built in 1974, about 49 years ago, which matters for roofs, plumbing and inspection requests. These numbers describe Seattle as a whole, so a given street can sit well above or below them.

Who bills property tax on a Seattle house?

King County bills and collects the tax on a Seattle house, and the city's own levies are added to the same county statement. Washington law makes the county treasurer the collector of all taxes on the roll, whether levied for the state, county, school district, city or another district (RCW 84.56.020). The King County Assessor sets the value and publishes the annual levy sheets that show how Seattle's rate is built.

Seattle is the county seat of King County and the most populous city in Washington, with 784,777 residents as of July 1, 2025. It sits on an isthmus between Puget Sound and Lake Washington, and the Census Bureau counts about 83.8 square miles of land. Only 43.7% of homes are owner-occupied, so most households rent. For 2020 to 2024 the median value of an owner-occupied home was $938,600 and median household income was $123,860.

Seattle's levy code in the King County rate book is 0010. If your parcel is in the city, the school district is almost always Seattle Public Schools, though a small part of the Delridge neighborhood falls inside the Highline School District.

Much of Seattle is hilly. Capitol Hill, First Hill, Queen Anne, Magnolia, West Seattle and Beacon Hill are among the hills the city is said to stand on, and neighborhoods such as Wallingford, Phinney Ridge, Maple Leaf and Madrona also sit on slopes. The climate is mild but wet: about 150 days a year bring measurable precipitation, and most of it falls between October and March.

What is the 2026 property tax rate in Seattle?

For 2026 the total levy rate for Seattle's levy code 0010 is $9.90845 per $1,000 of assessed value, up from $9.19418 in 2025. The King County Assessor's median-home sheet shows a typical Seattle home assessed at $833,000 for 2026 with a tax of $8,253.74. A year earlier the median assessed value was $864,000 and the tax was $7,943.77.

The sheet reports an average assessed value change of negative 3.6% for the city, an average tax rate change of 7.8% and an average tax change of 3.9%, or $309.97. In plain terms, values slipped while rates rose faster, so the average bill went up.

What changed on Seattle bills for 2026?

Voter-approved levies account for the largest line changes. Seattle School District 1 passed two special levies, a six-year capital levy and a three-year educational technology levy, and its capital line rose from 1.22694 to 1.41465 per $1,000. The city renewed its six-year families, education, preschool and promise levy and a ten-year election campaign voucher levy, and the promise line roughly doubled from 0.34844 to 0.68956.

King County voters also renewed several county measures that appear on every Seattle bill:

  • The automated fingerprint identification system levy, a seven-year renewal.
  • The parks, recreation, trails and open space levy, a six-year renewal.
  • The emergency medical services levy, a six-year renewal, with the EMS line moving from 0.22146 to 0.25098.
  • The county-wide hospital line, which went from 0.10000 to 0.15126.

The city levy lines for low-income housing, library services and the metro park district stayed close to their 2025 levels. If your 2026 bill looks different from the median figures above, check which school district and special districts your parcel is in.

When are Seattle property taxes due?

Under RCW 84.56.020, the first half of a Washington property tax bill is due on or before April 30 and the second half on or before October 31. When the total is $50 or more you may pay in two halves. The October 31, 2026 date has passed, so anyone with an unpaid second half should contact the King County treasurer for the current balance.

Late taxes on a residence with four or fewer units accrue interest at 9% a year, computed monthly, and state law bars penalties on those homes. Other property, including buildings with more than four units, pays 12% a year plus a 3% penalty on June 1 and an added 8% penalty on December 1. A treasurer may also offer payment agreements or accept partial payments, and the statute lets the treasurer extend due dates during a declared state of emergency.

Your tax statement should reach you by March 15 when the county has the roll in time. If you do not receive one, ask the King County treasurer for a copy.

How do I challenge a Seattle property assessment?

You petition the county board of equalization on forms approved by the Department of Revenue. RCW 84.40.038 sets the deadline as the later of July 1 of the assessment year, 30 days after the value notice was mailed or transmitted electronically, or a period of up to 60 days if the county legislative authority has adopted one. Read the deadline printed on your King County valuation notice, since the county may have chosen the longer window.

A board can accept a late petition if you file within a reasonable time and show good cause. The statute lists these circumstances.

  • Death or serious illness of the taxpayer or an immediate family member.
  • Absence from your usual address for more than fifteen of the days allowed.
  • Incorrect written filing advice from board or assessor staff.
  • A natural disaster such as a flood or earthquake.
  • A documented postal delay.

The board must also waive the deadline when you were never sent a revaluation notice even though your area was revalued and your value did not change.

What tax relief can Seattle homeowners claim?

The state senior and disabled exemption, RCW 84.36.381, can excuse part of the excess and regular levies on your home. To qualify you must own and live in the residence and be 61 or older on December 31 of the year you file, or retired from regular work because of disability, or a veteran receiving a service-connected rating of 40% or higher. A surviving spouse or domestic partner of a recipient can qualify at 57 or older. The amount depends on combined disposable income, so ask the King County Assessor for the current income thresholds.

The exemption can move with you. A claimant who sells, transfers or is displaced may carry the exemption status to a replacement residence, although only one residence per year can receive it. Deferred taxes, a separate program under chapter 84.38 RCW, become a lien repaid to the state with interest when ownership transfers.

How are property taxes and transfer tax handled when I sell in Seattle?

The tax is a lien on the property from January 1 of the levy year, and RCW 84.60.020 says that without a written agreement the seller is liable for the part of the year before the sale and the buyer for the rest. Escrow normally settles this at closing, along with any unpaid balance or deferral lien. Ask your escrow officer for a payoff figure before you sign a sale agreement.

The seller usually pays the state real estate excise tax, due to the county treasurer on the date of sale. For sales beginning January 1, 2027, the Department of Revenue lists 1.1% on the first $551,000, 1.28% from $551,000 to $1,551,000, 2.75% to $3,051,000 and 3% above. Applied to the $938,600 census median value, that comes to about $11,022 for the state share. The local excise tax is added, and Seattle's rate is one to confirm with your closing agent.

More questions about Seattle, WA Property Tax Guide

What is the Seattle property tax rate for 2026?

The total for levy code 0010 is $9.90845 per $1,000 of assessed value, according to the King County Assessor. A median home assessed at $833,000 carries about $8,253.74 in tax.

Does the City of Seattle send its own property tax bill?

No. The King County treasurer collects the tax for the city, the school district and every other district on one statement, as RCW 84.56.020 provides.

Is the second half of 2026 property tax still open?

The statutory due date of October 31 has passed. Contact the King County treasurer for the exact balance and any interest on an unpaid half.

Can I keep my senior exemption if I sell my Seattle house?

Often yes. RCW 84.36.381 lets a claimant transfer exemption status to a replacement residence, with one exempt home per year, so tell the assessor about the move.

Who pays property tax at closing in Seattle?

When the contract is silent, the seller owes the share of the year before the sale date and the buyer owes the remainder. Escrow handles the proration and pays any balance from the seller's proceeds.

Appeal petition to County Board of Equalization by July 1 of the assessment year or within 30 days of the Change of Value Notice mailing, whichever is later; no fee; petition form required.. See the official page.

Spokane by the numbers

Spokane has roughly 229,228 residents in the Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey, and ranks number 2 by population among the 51 Washington places in this guide. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $326,200 here, which is 35% below the middle figure for the 51 Washington places. About 42% of households rent, so 58% own; the Washington median for these places is 59% owner-occupied. Homes here were typically built in 1961, so the median house is about 62 years old. These numbers describe Spokane as a whole, so a given street can sit well above or below them.

Where is Spokane and how is the city laid out?

Spokane sits on the Spokane River in eastern Washington, less than 20 miles from the Idaho line, and it is the seat of Spokane County. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 230,783 residents, which makes it the second-largest city in the state after Seattle. The city was incorporated on November 29, 1881 and covers about 69 square miles at an elevation near 1,844 feet.

The street grid runs on the compass. Division Street splits the city into east and west, Sprague Avenue splits it into north and south, and Interstate 90 passes through. Downtown is the Riverside neighborhood, and the South Hill rises to the south. Browne's Addition, west of downtown, was the city's first prestigious address and holds Queen Anne and Craftsman mansions. Hillyard, in the northeast, grew around the Great Northern rail yard. West Central, East Central and the University District, where Gonzaga and the WSU Spokane health sciences campus sit, fill in the rest of the core.

Spokane Public Schools, organized in 1889, is the largest district in the city. The Mead district serves north Spokane County outside the city limits. Which district a house falls into changes its school levy, so check the address on the county's parcel record.

What do Spokane's housing numbers look like?

Spokane's owner-occupied rate is lower than the county's, so renters fill a larger share of homes. The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures set the city beside the county:

MeasureSpokane citySpokane County
Median owner-occupied home value$363,500$410,700
Owner-occupied housing rate58.8%64.5%
Median gross rent$1,215$1,283
Median household income$70,064$78,582
Households97,446218,395
Persons in poverty13.8%10.8%

Source: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts.

Climate is part of owning here. Spokane has cold winters and a dry summer pattern, with about 16.5 inches of precipitation a year. Drier summers and larger wildfires since the late 20th century have brought smoke that affects air quality. The warmest month is July at about 71 degrees on average and the coolest is December at about 29 degrees.

Who bills property tax for a Spokane house?

The city does not send the bill. The Spokane County Treasurer bills and collects the tax, and the Spokane County Assessor sets the value. The City of Spokane is one of the roughly 56 taxing districts in the county that send budgets to the Assessor each November.

City property tax goes mainly into the General Fund, which pays for police, fire, streets, parks and the library. The city's 2025 to 2026 proposed budget assumed it would levy the 1% increase allowed on regular levies, and it lists a streets levy and a public safety personnel levy fund among its dedicated revenue. Other lines on a Spokane bill come from the county, the school district, the state school levy and any special districts that cover the parcel.

Water, sewer, solid waste and other enterprise services are supported entirely by fees, not property tax. If you are selling, ask the city's utility billing office whether any utility balance is outstanding on the address.

  • Treasurer: Spokane County Courthouse, 1116 W. Broadway Ave., 509-477-4713, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
  • Assessor: 509-477-3698.
  • Mail payments to the Spokane County Treasurer, P.O. Box 199, Spokane, WA 99210.

When is Spokane property tax due?

Spokane property tax is due in two halves, April 30 and October 31, and a bill under $50 is due in full on April 30. If a date lands on a weekend or county holiday, the Treasurer accepts payment the next business day. The second half for 2026 was due October 31, 2026, so the next date on the calendar is April 30, 2027.

The statement arrives once a year with two coupons. If yours has not shown up by March 31, call 509-477-4713 or find it online on SCOUT. Mortgage companies may pay the tax from escrow, but the county says it does not bill them directly or keep their information, so confirm with your lender.

The courthouse has two drop boxes that accept checks only. On two Fridays and two Tuesdays before each due date, the Treasurer collects in person at Spokane Valley City Hall and the North Spokane Library. Mail is sorted by federal postmark, and the Treasurer warns that postal changes have delayed postmarks, so mail early. The office is closed Thursday and Friday, November 26 and 27, 2026.

What does late Spokane property tax cost?

Late tax in Spokane is charged interest beginning May 1 for the first half and November 1 for the second half, calculated on the full year's amount. A home with four or fewer units pays 0.75% per month and no penalty, while other property pays 1% per month plus a 3% penalty on June 1 and 8% on December 1.

State law gives the Treasurer discretion for payment agreements and partial payments on current and past-due taxes, with money applied to the oldest year first (RCW 84.56.020). A hardship waiver for a death of a spouse, parent or stepparent requires notice within 60 days of the due date (RCW 84.56.025). Spokane County says it cannot waive interest when the statement went to an address given by the taxpayer or the taxpayer's agent, such as a closing agent.

A payment that the bank returns carries a $30 fee, plus the interest, penalty and costs that apply.

How do you challenge a Spokane assessment?

Property in the city of Spokane is appealed through the Spokane County Board of Equalization, not through City Hall. File the petition form by July 1 of the assessment year or within 30 days after the Change of Value Notice was mailed, whichever is later. There is no fee, and a call or letter will not count in place of the form.

The board looks only at market value, and the assessor is presumed correct unless your evidence is clear, cogent and convincing (RCW 84.40.0301). Plan around these points:

  • The amount of tax, the percentage increase, other properties' values and personal hardship cannot be considered.
  • Comparable sales close to January 1 of the assessment year make the strongest case.
  • Additional evidence is due seven business days before the hearing.
  • The board gives notice of the hearing 15 business days ahead.

Talk to the Assessor first at 509-477-3698. Many disagreements end with a stipulation of value. If you lose, you have 30 calendar days to go to the State Board of Tax Appeals. The county Assessor revalues all parcels each year and inspects each one at least once every six years.

What relief exists for Spokane homeowners?

Seniors, people retired because of disability and certain veterans can apply for a property tax exemption through the Spokane County Assessor at 509-477-3698. The Treasurer's page says that Senate Bill 6162, signed after the 2026 session, will change the income thresholds starting in 2027, so ask about the limits that apply to you rather than relying on older numbers.

Every tax statement must carry a notice about the exemption and the state deferral program (RCW 84.56.020). Owners who are income-qualified, live in the home and face a tax foreclosure action can have interest and penalties waived about three years after delinquency, once, per property.

The county's Board of Equalization may also reconvene after the usual deadline when a buyer bought after July 1 and before December 31 of the assessment year for less than 90% of the assessed value.

What should you do about back taxes when selling in Spokane?

Ask the Treasurer for a payoff covering every year owed, give it to the closing agent, and confirm the agent has your correct parcel number and mailing address. Spokane County will not waive interest if its statement was mailed to the address a closing agent supplied.

Real estate excise tax is payable to the county treasurer on the date of sale, and the seller usually pays it. Under the Department of Revenue's schedule for sales from January 1, 2027, a sale at the city's $363,500 median home value falls entirely in the 1.1% state bracket, or $3,998.50, before the local rate is added.

Waiting can be risky. When tax stays unpaid three years after delinquency, the treasurer must start foreclosure by certificate of delinquency (RCW 84.64.050).

More questions about Spokane, WA Property Tax Guide

Who do I pay property tax to in Spokane?

The Spokane County Treasurer, at 1116 W. Broadway Ave. or P.O. Box 199, Spokane, WA 99210, or online. Call 509-477-4713. The city itself does not collect the tax.

When is Spokane property tax due?

April 30 and October 31, with bills under $50 due in full April 30. The October 31, 2026 date has passed, so the next one is April 30, 2027, or the following business day if that falls on a weekend.

How do I appeal my Spokane property value?

File a petition with the Spokane County Board of Equalization by July 1 of the assessment year or within 30 days of the Change of Value Notice, whichever is later. It is free, and you must show market value evidence, such as comparable sales.

What interest applies to late Spokane property tax?

For a home with four or fewer units, 0.75% a month with no penalty. For other property, 1% a month plus 3% on June 1 and 8% on December 1. The charge applies to the whole year's tax.

Can I sell a Spokane house that owes back taxes?

Yes. The unpaid tax, interest and penalties are paid from the proceeds at closing. Call the Spokane County Treasurer for a payoff, and give the closing agent your correct parcel number and mailing address.

Vancouver by the numbers

Vancouver has roughly 192,696 residents in the Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey, and ranks number 4 by population among the 51 Washington places in this guide. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $440,300 here, which is 12% below the middle figure for the 51 Washington places. About 50% of households rent, so 50% own; the Washington median for these places is 59% owner-occupied. Homes here were typically built in 1987, so the median house is about 36 years old. These numbers describe Vancouver as a whole, so a given street can sit well above or below them.

Which Clark County offices handle Vancouver property tax?

Clark County handles it, and its Treasurer, Assessor and Board of Equalization all work out of the Public Service Center at 1300 Franklin Street in downtown Vancouver. The Assessor values the property, the Treasurer bills and collects, and the Board hears value appeals.

  • Treasurer: 564.397.2252, treasoff@clark.wa.gov, in the second-floor Joint Lobby. The lobby is open Monday through Thursday from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and phone and email service runs Monday through Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Assessor: 564.397.2391, assessor@clark.wa.gov.
  • Board of Equalization: Suite 650, 564.397.2337, BOE@clark.wa.gov.

The county's Treasurer page lists the second-half 2026 due date as October 31, with a news release announcing payment on Monday, November 2 because the 31st fell on a Saturday. Neither date is still open.

What is Vancouver, Washington like for a seller?

Vancouver sits on the north bank of the Columbia River directly across from Portland, Oregon, and serves as the Clark County seat. Wikipedia traces it to Fort Vancouver, founded in 1825, with incorporation on January 23, 1857. World War II shipbuilding under Henry Kaiser pushed the population from about 18,000 to more than 80,000 within months, and neighborhoods such as Fruit Valley, Burton Homes and McLoughlin Heights grew from that wave of workers.

The 1997 annexation added 11,258 acres and 58,171 residents, and the city is often thought of as split into West and East Vancouver along NE Andresen Road. More than a third of the urban area's population lives in unincorporated areas just north of the city limits, including Hazel Dell, Felida, Orchards and Salmon Creek. Check your parcel on the county's Property Information Center to see whether it is inside city limits, because the levies differ.

  • Population: 199,698 in July 2025 on 48.74 square miles of land.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 50.8 percent.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $462,400.
  • Median gross rent: $1,702.
  • Median household income: $81,338.
  • Mean commute: 23.2 minutes, per the Census Bureau's QuickFacts.

What is the property tax rate in Vancouver?

Clark County's 2026 levy report puts the total levy for the tax area covering the City of Vancouver and Vancouver School District 37 (tax area 037000) at $9.6856 per $1,000 of assessed value. Other tax areas inside the city carry different districts, so the rate printed on your own statement is the one that applies.

Fort Vancouver Regional Library (general and capital facilities)0.5948

Source: Clark County 2026 Levy Rates Report by tax area. The library line adds the general rate of 0.5000 and the capital facilities rate of 0.0948. On a $500,000 assessment, the total works out to roughly $4,843 a year before exemptions.

When is Vancouver property tax due and what if it is late?

The first half or the full year is due April 30, and the second half is due October 31. A payment mailed on the due date counts only if the Postal Service postmarks it that day, and the county's FAQ page recommends handing it to a post office clerk rather than dropping it in a box. Paying by e-check online is free and is another way to pay on the due date itself. Statements for the first half are usually available by March 15, and for the second half by September 15.

Late interest follows state law. For tax years 2023 and later on a residential parcel with four or fewer units, the county charges 0.75 percent per month with no penalty. Other parcels pay 1 percent per month plus penalties of 3 percent on June 1 and 8 percent on December 1.

  • Real property that is three or more years delinquent is subject to foreclosure under chapter 84.64 RCW.
  • Once court proceedings start, all taxes, interest, penalties and foreclosure costs must be paid in full before the auction date.
  • When a certificate of delinquency has been filed, the Treasurer accepts payments only from owners and recorded interests.
  • An income-qualified owner-occupant facing foreclosure can ask for a one-time waiver of interest and penalties under RCW 84.56.020(19).

If you are behind, email taxrequests@clark.wa.gov or call 564.397.2252 before you list the home.

Does your mortgage escrow pay Vancouver property tax?

More than 45 percent of Clark County homeowners pay through escrow, according to the Treasurer's Mortgage and Escrow page. If you are one of them, the county does not mail you a statement, and you remain responsible for confirming payment after each installment is due.

The county says lenders sometimes pay the wrong account number or miss a payment. Check the taxes tab on the Property Information Center after April 30 and October 31. If a delinquency notice arrives, ask the lender which account numbers it paid and request a copy of the cancelled check or disbursement record. The county also warns against paying twice, so confirm with the lender before sending your own payment.

How do you appeal a Vancouver property value?

Appeal to the Clark County Board of Equalization within 60 calendar days of the mailing date on your Notice of Value, or by July 1, whichever is later. The county's Board of Equalization page says late appeals cannot be accepted, and it counts 60 days from the notice date rather than two months. You can also file a preemptive appeal from January 1 through July 1 of the assessment year.

The Assessor mails most Notices of Value in June and the rest in September, and only properties whose value changed receive one. The appeal is free. A three-member citizen board hears each case in a 15-minute hearing and mails a written decision within 30 days. The county reports that historically more than half of appeals end favorably for the owner, either after talking with the Assessor or at a hearing.

  • Best evidence: comparable sales or a recent appraisal, repair bids and photographs.
  • Other properties' assessed values are not a persuasive argument.
  • Extra evidence must reach the Board 21 business days before the hearing.
  • A decision can be appealed to the State Board of Tax Appeals.

What relief and closing steps apply to a Vancouver sale?

Clark County's senior exemption has three income tiers. For tax years 2024 through 2026 the top income limit is $62,000, rising for 2027 to 2029 to $85,000 under Senate Bill 6162, according to the county's exemption FAQ. For 2027, applicants must be 61 or older, unable to work because of a disability, or a veteran with a disability rating of 40 percent or higher, and must own the home and live in it at least six months of the year. Applications for 2027 open in February 2027, and current participants are adjusted automatically.

At closing, RCW 84.60.020 attaches the tax lien on January 1 and, absent a contract term, prorates the year by the sale date. Ask your escrow officer to confirm both halves with the Treasurer, and check with the Assessor whether an exemption or deferral will end with the sale.

More questions about Vancouver, WA Property Tax Guide

When is Vancouver, WA property tax due?

April 30 for the first half or full year, and October 31 for the second half. In 2026 October 31 fell on a Saturday, and the Clark County Treasurer announced payment on Monday, November 2. That date has passed.

What interest does Clark County charge on late property tax?

For tax years 2023 and later on a residential parcel with four or fewer units, 0.75 percent per month and no penalties. Other parcels pay 1 percent per month plus 3 percent on June 1 and 8 percent on December 1.

How long before Clark County forecloses for unpaid taxes?

Three years. Real property with taxes three or more years delinquent is subject to foreclosure under chapter 84.64 RCW. Call the Treasurer at 564.397.2252 or email taxrequests@clark.wa.gov to discuss relief.

How long do I have to appeal my Vancouver assessment?

Sixty calendar days from the mailing date on your Notice of Value, or July 1 if later. Late appeals cannot be accepted. Contact the Board of Equalization at 564.397.2337 or BOE@clark.wa.gov.

Is my Vancouver address inside city limits?

Not always. Hazel Dell, Felida, Orchards and Salmon Creek are unincorporated communities north of the city limits. Look up your parcel on the Clark County Property Information Center to see which tax area applies.

content:
Tacoma, WA Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Washington
Cash Offer in 24 Hours

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Tacoma, WA Property Tax Guide sale

Owe Tacoma Property Tax? Get a Cash Offer

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Tacoma property tax is billed by the offices named below.

Who bills what in Tacoma

  • Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer's Office handles assessment.
  • Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer's Office bills and collects the tax.

Due dates

First half due April 30; second half due Oct. 31, which falls on a weekend in 2026 so it is due Monday, Nov. 2, 2026 (FAQ opened).. See the official page.

Challenging your assessment

Petition to the independent Pierce County Board of Equalization: by July 1 or within 60 days of the mailing of the value change notice (deadline wording from search excerpts of the Appeals and BOE pages; extraction of the opened pages did not return the text).. See the official page.

Tax rate

We could not confirm the current Tacoma rate on an opened page, so we do not state one.

Local notes

  • Census Vintage 2025 population 229816; county from Census sub-est2025_53 SUMLEV 157.
  • Pierce is the one Washington county here where the Assessor and Treasurer are a combined office.
Behind on Tacoma property tax?
We buy Tacoma houses as-is, and the title company pays unpaid tax from the proceeds.
Get My Cash Offer →

Tacoma by the numbers

Tacoma has roughly 220,482 residents in the Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey, and ranks number 3 by population among the 51 Washington places in this guide. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $454,600 here, which is 9% below the middle figure for the 51 Washington places. About 44% of households rent, so 56% own; the Washington median for these places is 59% owner-occupied. Homes here were typically built in 1967, so the median house is about 56 years old. These numbers describe Tacoma as a whole, so a given street can sit well above or below them.

Who sends the property tax bill in Tacoma?

Pierce County sends it. Tacoma is the county seat of Pierce County, and the county's Assessor-Treasurer's Office both values your home and collects the tax.

  • Pay or check a balance: Pierce County Annex, 2401 S 35th Street, Room 142, Tacoma, with a drop box for after-hours payments.
  • Customer service: (253) 798-6111.
  • Automated tax and value line: (253) 798-3333, which takes card and e-check payments with a parcel number.
  • Foreclosure avoidance payments: a cashier's check to Pierce County, marked Attention: Foreclosure Avoidance, at the same Room 142 address.

Tacoma's own levy is part of the combined rate, and the county mails the statement in February and collects the whole bill, as described on the county's Tax Bills and Payments page.

What should a Tacoma home seller know about the city?

Tacoma is a port city on Puget Sound about 30 miles from both Seattle and Olympia, and it is the third most populous city in Washington. Wikipedia records that the city was incorporated on November 12, 1875, after the Northern Pacific Railroad chose the area as its western terminus, and that the older settlement merged with New Tacoma in January 1884. The Port of Tacoma on Commencement Bay is the state's largest port, and downtown has seen revitalization since the 1990s, including the University of Washington Tacoma and the T Line light rail.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table puts Tacoma at 229,816 residents in July 2025 on 49.71 square miles, roughly 4,412 people per square mile.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 55.8 percent.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $479,600.
  • Median gross rent: $1,676.
  • Median household income: $85,884.
  • Mean commute: 28.8 minutes.

About 44 percent of Tacoma households rent, which matters if the house you are selling has a tenant in it.

When is Tacoma property tax due?

Half is due by April 30 and the other half by October 31, and Pierce County's 2026 notice listed the second installment as November 2. Tax statements are mailed in February. If the amount is $50 or less, the whole bill is due April 30. Failure to receive a statement does not waive interest on a late tax.

Mailed payments should be postmarked by the due date. The county suggests certified mail with a return receipt so you hold proof of the postmark, and it will waive interest if the envelope's postmark shows the payment was mailed before the deadline. A payment that arrives late without the correct interest is returned. Mortgage companies follow the same rules as individual owners and are expected to pay every tax, assessment and charge on the parcel.

November 2, 2026 has passed. If you were counting on the second half being open, call (253) 798-6111 for the balance and any interest that has started.

What is the Tacoma tax rate?

Pierce County's 2026 average rate for Tacoma's tax code area 005 is $10.876 per $1,000 of assessed value. It is a combined per-$1,000 figure for the whole area. On a home assessed at $500,000, it comes to roughly $5,438 a year before any exemption. Your own parcel can differ slightly, since the figure is an average for the tax code area, so check the rate on your statement.

Assessments follow a calendar the county explains on its residential appeals page. Values are set as of January 1, based on sales before that date, so the 2026 assessment draws on 2025 sales and sets the base for taxes due in 2027.

What if you fall behind on Tacoma property tax?

Interest at 0.75 percent per month is charged on the full year's tax beginning May 1 for residential properties with one to four units, for tax year 2023 and later. Penalties of 3 percent and 8 percent apply only to other property types, so a single-family house does not accrue them. Monthly payment plans are available through the Assessor-Treasurer, and the county's payment plan page sets out the terms:

  • A current-tax escrow plan costs $100 to set up and $15 a month.
  • A delinquent-tax plan costs $100 to set up and $17 a month and can run up to 18 months.
  • The oldest outstanding tax must be paid in full by April 30 of the year it turns three years delinquent.

Foreclosure is the next step. The county's foreclosure page says properties with more than $100 in cumulative tax that is three or more years delinquent are foreclosed through a Certificate of Delinquency filed with Pierce County Superior Court. The 2026 auction was set for Monday, November 9, and that date has passed. Call (253) 798-2728 to ask about plans.

How do you appeal a Tacoma property value?

File a petition with the Pierce County Board of Equalization by July 1 or within 60 days of the date the value change notice was mailed. The board accepts only Washington Department of Revenue petition forms, and it takes one parcel per petition.

  • The question is market value on January 1. Tax amount, percentage increases, comparisons to neighbors and personal hardship are not considered.
  • Useful evidence includes comparable sales from the right year, contractor bids to fix defects, easement documents, independent appraisals and photographs.
  • A petition that only says the value or tax is too high is rejected.
  • Any evidence not filed with the petition goes to the board at least 21 business days before the hearing.

The Assessor-Treasurer's value is presumed correct, so you carry the burden of proof. The board is at 2401 S 35th St, Room 176, phone (253) 798-7415. State law at RCW 84.40.038 sets the baseline deadlines and lists good-cause reasons a board may accept a late petition.

What tax relief and closing taxes apply in Tacoma?

Pierce County's January 2026 mailing says seniors and people with disabilities may apply for an exemption that can freeze taxable value and remove some levies. You must be at least 61 or awarded disability status by December 31 of the previous year, earn no more than $64,000 after allowable deductions, own the home by December 31 of the assessment year, live in it more than six months of the prior year, and file an application.

When you sell, the excise tax is a separate bill from property tax. The Pierce County Auditor's rate sheet lists the state graduated rate and a local rate that applies in Tacoma:

Sale priceState excise rate
Up to $525,0001.1 percent
$525,000.01 to $1,525,0001.28 percent
$1,525,000.01 to $3,025,0002.75 percent
Above $3,025,0003 percent

Source: Pierce County Auditor excise tax rate sheet for sales on or after January 1, 2023. The same sheet adds a 0.50 percent local rate for Tacoma. Property tax is prorated by the sale date under RCW 84.60.020, with the lien attaching each January 1, so ask your escrow officer to confirm the open half with the Assessor-Treasurer.

More questions about Tacoma, WA Property Tax Guide

Who do I pay Tacoma property tax to?

The Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer. Pay online, by phone at (253) 798-3333, by mail to Pierce County Finance, or in person at 2401 S 35th Street, Room 142 in Tacoma. Make checks payable to Pierce County.

What is the interest on late Tacoma property tax?

For a residential property with four or fewer units, 0.75 percent per month on the full year's tax starting May 1, for tax year 2023 and later. Other property types also face 3 percent and 8 percent penalties.

How long can Tacoma property tax go unpaid before foreclosure?

Three years. Pierce County forecloses on parcels with more than $100 in cumulative tax that is three or more years delinquent. The county's 2026 sale date was November 9, which has passed.

What is the deadline to appeal a Tacoma assessment?

July 1 of the assessment year, or 60 days after the mailing date of your value change notice, filed with the Pierce County Board of Equalization. A copy of the notice is required if you file after July 1.

Do I pay excise tax when I sell a house in Tacoma?

Yes. The state graduated excise rate applies to the sale, and the Pierce County Auditor's sheet adds a 0.50 percent local rate for Tacoma. Ask your escrow officer for the exact figure at your sale price.
